question: In 1596, who suggested in his work ‘Thesaurus Geographicus' that the continents of the earth were not always located in their present positions?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Abraham Ortelius**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• **Abraham Ortelius** suggested in his work 'Thesaurus Geographicus' in 1596 that the continents of the Earth were not always located in their present positions.
 
• Ortelius was a pioneering cartographer and geographer who is often credited with the early concept of continental drift.
